newsitem.title: UK: NatWest sees 2-3 billion stg UK tightening.
newsitem.headline: NatWest sees 2-3 billion stg UK tightening.

text.p: National Westminster Bank Plc group chief economist David Kern said he expected a net fiscal tightening of at least two to three billion stg in the new Labour government's first budget on July 2.

The budget deficit was arguably too high for the current phase of the economic cycle and a fiscal tightening would help to slow down the current consumer-driven, above-trend economic growth to more sustainable levels, he said.
"Fiscal tightening will clearly have to be implemented through higher taxation rather than spending cuts," Kern said.
The most significant revenue-gathering measures are likely to be scrapping or restricting tax relief on mortgage interest payments and cuts in advance corporation tax (ACT), he added.
Cutting ACT actually raises tax revenue by limiting the ability of pension funds and other tax exempt bodies to claim back tax from the exchequer.
Kern said reducing ACT could lead to a fall in share prices, as happened when it was cut in 1993, and force companies to boost contributions to their pension funds.

Other possible measures could include restricting tax relief on pension contributions to the basic rate of tax, reducing the tax breaks on Personal Equity Plans (PEPs) and Tax Exempt Special Savings Accounts (TESSAs), scrapping the married couples' allowance and abolishing tax relief on private medical insurance premiums for the over-65s.
"One further potential area for revenue gathering is green' taxation, for example energy taxes on business, a waste disposal tax and extra increases in petrol duty," Kern said.
